key_insight: A time-level mismatch in momentum convection creates spurious near-surface currents; explicit convection with upwind interface velocities removes the mismatch.
engineering_relevance: Consistent momentum transport improves two-phase wave predictions while reducing wall-clock time by 34–42% versus interFoam for the tested wave.
method: Identify the lag between interface-advection mass flux and implicitly convected velocity.
Use explicit momentum convection with upwind face velocities at the interface.
Validate with prescribed flows and full-solver progressive-wave simulations.
evidence_signal: For a progressive wave, fluxinator reduced crest-velocity overprediction from 26–31% to within 1% and kept wave height within 1.5% over 15 periods on meshes with at least six cells per wave height.
watch_item: The solver is intended for maximum Courant numbers of 0.1 or below; performance at larger time steps is not established here.
paper_title: Consistent interfacial flow numerics - Part II: The momentum convection term
